query: How do we define a negative-transfer diagnostic suite and thresholds (negative transfer index, per-output domain-gap, degradation rate) to detect harmful transfer early in experiments?

response.query: How do we define a negative-transfer diagnostic suite and thresholds (negative transfer index, per-output domain-gap, degradation rate) to detect harmful transfer early in experiments?
response.answer: A negative-transfer diagnostic suite includes metrics like the negative transfer index, per-output domain-gap, and degradation rate to detect harmful transfer early in experiments. These metrics quantify performance decline and domain shifts. Thresholds for these metrics are set based on empirical observations and domain-specific benchmarks.

results.title: Colloquium | Department of Physics
results.content: I lead the Quantum Layered Matter Group at Tel Aviv University, where we investigate electronic and structural phases in two-dimensional (2D) materials, primarily through low-temperature transport and surface probe microscopy. In the talk I will review this topic, show some results (D-wave and laser systems), discuss what we do/don't understand, and try to provide some intuition on what physical mechanisms are expected to give real benefits. I will show both ionization-induced dynamics that are initiated by ultrafast EUV pulses,[1] as well dynamics that are initiated by the mutual neutralization of molecular anions and cations in merged-beams experiments.[2,3] Furthermore, I will discuss our efforts to achieve direct comparison of experimental and theoretical studies towards a better understanding of time-evolving small quantum systems. Kumar, et al., Interaction-driven quantum phase transitions between topological and crystalline orders of electrons, *arXiv*: 2504.18626 More recently, the structure of grain boundaries has been described following diffuse interface theory, stating that the structure and chemistry of grain boundaries, interfaces and surfaces can go through two dimensional transitions between thermodynamic states (termed *complexions*) in order to lower the interface energy.
